source: Public App Store screenshots and apple.com/apple-card, collected 2026-11-26. Pictures are not kept in the repo.

screens.why: One number: 2,272 left of 5,400. Under it one line, spending pace against the budget line. Nothing else competes.
A plain table: category, average spent, budget, in right-aligned columns. The total sits under it once.
New transactions arrive as a short queue with suggested categories; you approve. The machine suggests, you decide.
Net income as the headline, then one bar per month. The single red month is the only colour that shouts.
Bills due this month: one ring of paid so far, then a grid of each bill with its date.
Plain-language notes about spending. Useful, but close to the AI-chat look you dislike.
Left to budget sits in a green band at the top. Income, expenses and goals are each one bar with spent and remaining in words.
A Sankey answers one question, where every krone went, in one picture.
Reviewing a transaction is a card you throw aside. Routine work turned into one gesture.
Upcoming bills with 'in 10 days' beside each. Time left matters more than the date.
A goal is a photo card with its progress. Warm, but the photo carries the feeling, not the data.
Editorial serif headlines with italics give the brand a voice; the app itself stays plain.
Every category one row, available money in a green pill on the right. 'Ready to Assign' is the one number at the top.
Overspent is a red card with the amount and the next step: pick where to take the money from. No dead end.
A new transaction is a card to approve with a swipe.
232 kr available in Groceries. One category, one number, one answer, on the lock screen.
Income against spending per month on dark, one sentence of verdict above the bars.
A goal's balance as a short ledger: from July, assigned, activity, available.
Monospace figures everywhere: nerdy, honest, a ledger feel. Dense, with almost no hierarchy.
Grouped by day, payee and category stacked, amount right. Fast to scan.
Every category a thin bar with its amount. Readable, but nothing stands out.
A single big count, then a line. Shows how a lone figure can lead a screen.
A huge balance over a photo, four round actions, then a short list of what happened.
Two people in the photo behind a shared balance: sharing made human.
Payments as a chat with a person. Money between people reads like a conversation.
On payday, rules sort the salary into pots. Salary as the start of the month.
A big balance with a quiet area chart, then tasks waiting for you. Calm, lots of air.
Spent this month against the limit as one bar, then posted, pending, available as labelled rows.
The amount large at the top, then category, notes and receipt below. One thing per screen.
Dark, grainy, a thin line chart and one balance. Premium without decoration.
Inbox, needs approval, scheduled: work sorted by what you must do next.
Balance and payment due side by side, weekly activity as small bars coloured by category.
A dial you drag to see what paying more saves. Money made tangible in one gesture.
Paid against remaining as one bar, history below. Nothing extra.
A balance, a line, two buttons, latest transactions. The iOS grouped style done right.
Status as small icons in one column, nothing boxed, calm density. Structure from alignment.
One list, a two-way filter at the top, each row its avatar and one line.
Properties as quiet chips, then sections. Lots of information, no noise.
Colour only where it means a place. Generous white, soft type, one blue button.
Calendar events on top, to-dos under, an evening section. Time of day structures the list.
Days as big numerals with items beneath. A date can be the design.
A new item expands in place over the list; Save sits where your thumb is.
Dark mode tuned, not inverted: the same calm in the other light.
'Overall, you owe 287.49' in words, then per group who owes whom, owe in orange and owed in green with the words.
'Paid by you and split equally' is one tappable sentence. The split is a sentence, not a form.
You, an arrow, Earl, the amount. One picture of who pays whom.
Who paid and each person's share in one indented list.
'623 left to spend' with '48 per day for 13 days'. A daily allowance makes the cycle concrete.
Bills in the next 7 days on a week strip. The near future, not a calendar.
Month bars with a period switch, then income, spend and net as rows.
A bird mascot and 'AI-powered' in the headline: the look to avoid.
'Payday to payday budgeting': a ring of 2,067 left of 3,500. The cycle idea, in a generic shell.
Purple, stars, accounts as rows. Busy and generic: an example of 'a good app, just as an app'.
Logos, amounts and cadence in a clean list. The logos carry recognition.
